questions.stem: In a six-figure grid reference such as 345678 on a topographic map, the first three figures give the:
options: bearing of the point from true north
easting, read along the bottom or top of the map
northing, read up the side of the map
altitude of the point above sea level
questions.explanation: Grid references always give the easting first (the vertical grid line, numbered along the bottom) and then the northing. A common memory aid is 'along the corridor, then up the stairs'.

questions.stem: On a topographic map, a church lies inside the grid square bounded by eastings 23 and 24 and northings 61 and 62. Its four-figure area reference is:
questions.explanation: An area reference names the square by the easting and northing of its bottom-left (south-west) corner, easting first. Using the top or right-hand lines, or putting the northing first, gives the wrong square.

questions.stem: A trig station lies three-tenths of the way east from easting 52 towards easting 53, and seven-tenths of the way north from northing 18 towards northing 19. Its six-figure grid reference is:
questions.explanation: The easting comes first: 52 plus three-tenths gives 523. The northing is 18 plus seven-tenths, giving 187. Swapping the tenths, or putting the northing first, are the usual slips.

questions.stem: On a map, the latitude lines 34°00'S and 34°10'S are 12 cm apart. A homestead lies 3 cm north of the 34°10'S line. Its latitude is closest to:
questions.explanation: Ten minutes of latitude span 12 cm, so 3 cm is a quarter of that, or 2.5 minutes. In the Southern Hemisphere latitude decreases northwards, so the homestead is at 34°10' minus 2.5', which is 34°07.5'S.

questions.stem: On a topographic map, contour lines that are very close together indicate:
options: a flat plateau
a river valley floor
a steep slope
a gentle slope
questions.explanation: Each contour line joins places of equal height, so close spacing means height changes quickly over a short horizontal distance. Widely spaced contours show gentle slopes or flat land.

questions.stem: Down a hillside, the contours are closely spaced near the summit and become widely spaced towards the valley floor. The slope is best described as:
options: uniform, with the same gradient all the way down
a cliff, with a vertical drop near the summit
concave, steep at the top and gentle at the bottom
convex, gentle at the top and steep at the bottom
questions.explanation: Close contours high up mean the upper slope is steep; wide spacing lower down means the lower slope is gentle, which is a concave profile. A convex slope has the reverse pattern, with contours crowding towards the bottom.

questions.stem: Where contour lines cross a creek on a topographic map, they bend into a V shape. The point of the V shows that:
options: the V points downstream, towards the river mouth
the V points north, because contours face north
the V points to the steepest side of the valley
the V points upstream, towards higher ground
questions.explanation: A valley cuts back into the land, so each contour bends upstream before crossing the creek. This is one way to work out the direction of river flow, which is away from the point of the V.

questions.stem: The highest point on a map extract is a spot height of 486 m and the lowest is a river at 112 m. The local relief is:
questions.explanation: Local relief is the difference between the highest and lowest points: 486 minus 112 equals 374 m. Adding the two heights gives 598 m, which is not relief.

questions.stem: A road climbs 150 m over a horizontal distance of 3 km. Its average gradient is:
questions.explanation: Gradient is rise over run in the same units: 150 m over 3 000 m simplifies to 1:20. Forgetting to convert kilometres to metres gives 1:2, and writing the ratio the wrong way gives 20:1.

questions.stem: On a 1:25 000 map, a walking track runs from the 220 m contour to the 320 m contour. The two points are 4 cm apart on the map. The average gradient is:
questions.explanation: At 1:25 000, 4 cm represents 100 000 cm, or 1 000 m. The rise is 100 m, so the gradient is 100:1 000, or 1:10. Treating 4 cm as 4 km gives 1:40.

questions.stem: A cross-section is drawn from a 1:25 000 map with a vertical scale of 1 cm to 50 m. The vertical exaggeration is:
options: 0.2 times
50 times
500 times
5 times
questions.explanation: Convert both scales to ratios: the vertical scale of 1 cm to 5 000 cm is 1:5 000. Vertical exaggeration is the horizontal scale divided by the vertical scale, so 25 000 / 5 000 = 5. Dividing the other way gives 0.2.

questions.stem: Why is a vertical exaggeration usually applied when drawing a cross-section from a topographic map?
options: It converts the horizontal scale of the map into the same units as the contours
Heights are small compared with horizontal distances, so relief would look too flat
It makes the gradients on the cross-section exactly the same as those on the ground
It removes the need to plot the contour heights accurately along the section line
questions.explanation: Over several kilometres, a relief of a few hundred metres would be almost invisible at true scale, so heights are stretched to show the landforms. The trade-off is that slopes look steeper than they really are.

questions.stem: A walking track measures 18 cm on a 1:50 000 map. Walking at 4 km/h, about how long will the walk take?
options: 13 minutes 30 seconds
2 hours 15 minutes
2 hours 25 minutes
4 hours 30 minutes
questions.explanation: At 1:50 000, 1 cm represents 0.5 km, so 18 cm is 9 km. Time = distance / speed = 9 / 4 = 2.25 hours, which is 2 hours 15 minutes, not 2 hours 25 minutes.

questions.stem: In New South Wales, which aspect receives the most direct sunlight, especially in winter?
options: east-facing
west-facing
north-facing
south-facing
questions.explanation: South of the Tropic of Capricorn the midday sun is always in the northern sky, so north-facing slopes are warmer and drier. South-facing slopes are shadier, cooler and often moister.

questions.stem: The bearing from a homestead to a dam is 060°. What is the bearing from the dam back to the homestead?
questions.explanation: A back bearing differs by 180°: 060 + 180 = 240°. Subtracting from 360° gives 300°, which is a common error.

questions.stem: Point B lies exactly south-west of point A. The bearing from A to B is:
questions.explanation: Bearings are measured clockwise from north: east is 090°, south 180° and south-west halfway between south and west at 225°. 135° is south-east.

questions.stem: An observer stands at a lookout at 300 m. A tower at 280 m lies 3 km away, and a ridge rising to 340 m lies between them. Can the observer see the tower?
options: No, because the ridge rises above the line of sight between them
Yes, because the lookout is higher than the base of the tower
Yes, because sight lines are only blocked by features over 500 m
No, because nothing can be seen from more than 2 km away
questions.explanation: A sight line is blocked if any land between the two points rises above the straight line joining them. Here the ridge at 340 m is higher than both the lookout and the tower, so the view is blocked.

questions.stem: A rectangular nature reserve measures 6 cm by 4 cm on a 1:50 000 map. Its area on the ground is:
options: 60 km²
6 km²
24 km²
1.5 km²
questions.explanation: At 1:50 000, 1 cm represents 0.5 km, so the reserve is 3 km by 2 km, or 6 km². Multiplying the map measurements gives 24, and using the 1:25 000 conversion gives 1.5 km².

questions.stem: A map extract at 1:25 000 measures 8 cm by 6 cm and contains 54 houses. The housing density is:
options: 18 houses per km²
27 houses per km²
1.1 houses per km²
4.5 houses per km²
questions.explanation: At 1:25 000, 1 cm represents 0.25 km, so the extract is 2 km by 1.5 km, or 3 km². Density = 54 / 3 = 18 houses per km². Dividing by the map area of 48 cm² gives 1.1.

questions.stem: Which data set is most appropriate to show on a choropleth map of local government areas?
options: population density in people per km²
the location of each public hospital
the route of the main inland highway
the flow of commuters between areas
questions.explanation: A choropleth map shades whole areas according to a value per area or a rate, such as density. Point locations suit dot maps, routes suit line maps and movements suit flow-line maps.

questions.stem: On a synoptic chart, isobars packed closely together around a low-pressure system indicate:
options: a heatwave
strong winds
calm, clear weather
high air pressure
questions.explanation: Isobars join places of equal air pressure. Close spacing means a steep pressure gradient, which drives strong winds. Widely spaced isobars around a high usually mean light winds and settled weather.

questions.stem: In the Southern Hemisphere, how does air circulate around a high-pressure system on a weather map?
options: clockwise and outwards from the centre
anticlockwise and outwards from the centre
clockwise and inwards towards the centre
anticlockwise and inwards towards the centre
questions.explanation: Air sinks in a high and spreads out, and the Coriolis effect turns it anticlockwise in the Southern Hemisphere. Lows in the Southern Hemisphere rotate clockwise with air converging inwards.

questions.stem: On a summer afternoon a cold front crosses the coast of New South Wales. What change is most likely as the front passes?
options: temperature falls and the wind swings to the south
temperature rises and the wind swings to the north
pressure falls steadily and the sky clears completely
humidity drops to zero and the wind stops entirely
questions.explanation: Ahead of a cold front, warm northerly or north-westerly winds are common. As it passes, cooler air arrives with a southerly change, often gusty, and temperatures drop sharply.

questions.stem: A town's population grew from 40 000 in 2011 to 46 000 in 2021. The average rate of increase was:
options: 1 500 people per year
600 people per year
6 000 people per year
4 600 people per year
questions.explanation: The rate of increase is the change divided by the time: 6 000 people over 10 years is 600 people per year. 6 000 is the total change, not the annual rate.

questions.stem: Annual rainfall at a station fell from 800 mm to 600 mm. Which correctly states the absolute and proportional change?
options: a fall of 200 mm, or 25%
a fall of 200 mm, or 33%
a fall of 25 mm, or 200%
a rise of 200 mm, or 25%
questions.explanation: The absolute change is 600 minus 800, a fall of 200 mm. The proportional change is 200 divided by the original 800, which is 25%. Dividing by the new value of 600 gives 33%.

questions.stem: On a map of proportional circles, circle X has twice the radius of circle Y. If circle Y represents 5 000 tonnes, circle X represents about:
options: 40 000 tonnes
20 000 tonnes
10 000 tonnes
2 500 tonnes
questions.explanation: In proportional circles the area, not the radius, is proportional to the value. Area depends on the radius squared, so doubling the radius gives four times the area: 4 x 5 000 = 20 000 tonnes.

questions.stem: On a pie graph representing 250 000 visitors, one sector has an angle of 72°. How many visitors does the sector represent?
options: 25 000 visitors
50 000 visitors
72 000 visitors
36 000 visitors
questions.explanation: A sector's share is its angle divided by 360°: 72 / 360 = 0.2, and 0.2 x 250 000 = 50 000. Reading the angle as a number of thousands gives 72 000.

questions.stem: Region A's proportional divided circle shows exports of 400 000 t, of which 30% is coal. Region B's circle shows 200 000 t, of which 50% is coal. Which statement is correct?
options: Region A exports 20 000 t more coal than Region B
Region B exports more coal because its share is larger
Both regions export exactly the same tonnage of coal
Region A exports twice as much coal as Region B
questions.explanation: Region A exports 0.3 x 400 000 = 120 000 t and Region B 0.5 x 200 000 = 100 000 t, a difference of 20 000 t. With circles of different sizes, a larger percentage does not mean a larger amount.

questions.stem: A population profile has a narrow base and a bulge in the 40 to 64 age groups. This most likely indicates:
options: high death rates among middle-aged adults
rapid population growth from natural increase
low birth rates and an ageing population
high birth rates and a youthful population
questions.explanation: A narrow base means fewer children are being born than in earlier decades, and the bulge shows large cohorts moving into older age. A youthful, fast-growing population would have a wide base.

questions.stem: A scatter graph of median land value against distance from the CBD shows points falling from top left to bottom right. This shows:
options: no correlation between land value and distance
that distance from the CBD is the only cause of value
a negative correlation: land value falls with distance
a positive correlation: land value rises with distance
questions.explanation: Points sloping downward to the right mean that as one variable increases the other decreases, a negative correlation. A correlation alone does not prove that distance causes the change in value.

questions.stem: On a ternary graph showing the share of employment in primary, secondary and tertiary industries, a country plots at 10% primary and 30% secondary. Its tertiary share is:
questions.explanation: The three components of a ternary graph always add to 100%, so tertiary = 100 - 10 - 30 = 60%. Adding only two values, or subtracting one, gives the other options.

questions.stem: Daily rainfall at a station over a year is mostly 0 to 5 mm, with a few days over 100 mm. Which statistic best represents a typical day's rainfall?
options: the total, as it includes the rainfall of every single day
the median, as the mean is pulled up by a few very wet days
the mean, as it is always the most typical value of any data set
the range, as it shows the spread between the extreme values
questions.explanation: In a positively skewed distribution, a few extreme values drag the mean upwards, while the median, the middle value, is not affected by them. The range and total describe spread and amount, not a typical value.

questions.stem: A GPS receiver works out the location of a fieldwork site by:
options: comparing a photograph of the site with an aerial image
measuring the distance to the nearest trig station by laser
receiving timing signals from several orbiting satellites
measuring the strength of the Earth's magnetic field there
questions.explanation: A GPS receiver calculates its position from the time signals take to arrive from at least four satellites. A compass uses the magnetic field but cannot give a position on its own.

questions.stem: A planner overlays a flood-extent layer on a layer of property boundaries in a GIS. The main purpose is to:
options: record the rainfall total at each property during a flood
identify which properties lie within the flood-prone area
measure how fast floodwater travels along the river channel
predict the exact date of the next major flood in the area
questions.explanation: A GIS stores data as layers that can be overlaid to show spatial relationships, such as which properties fall inside a mapped hazard zone. Flow speed and flood dates need hydrological models and records, not an overlay.

questions.stem: Satellite images show that urban land in a district covered 25 km² in 2004 and 40 km² in 2024. The proportional increase is:
questions.explanation: The change is 15 km², and 15 divided by the original 25 is 0.6, or 60%. Dividing by the final area gives 37.5%, and 160% is the 2024 area as a percentage of 2004.

questions.stem: A sports field known to be 120 m long measures 2.4 cm on a vertical aerial photograph. The approximate scale of the photograph is:
questions.explanation: Convert to the same units: 120 m is 12 000 cm, and 12 000 / 2.4 = 5 000, so 1 cm on the photo represents 5 000 cm. Ignoring the 2.4 cm gives 1:12 000.

questions.stem: A photograph taken in New South Wales shows long shadows pointing towards the west. It was most likely taken in the:
options: summer at midday
early morning
late afternoon
middle of the day
questions.explanation: Shadows point away from the sun. Long shadows to the west mean a low sun in the east, which is early morning. In the late afternoon the sun is in the west and shadows point east; around midday they are short and point south.

questions.stem: In a 60 ha study area on an aerial photograph, cropland covers 36 ha, grazing land 18 ha and forest 6 ha. The ratio of cropland to grazing to forest is:
questions.explanation: Divide each area by the smallest, 6 ha: 36/6 = 6, 18/6 = 3 and 6/6 = 1, giving 6:3:1. The ratio keeps the order in which the land uses are named.

questions.stem: A précis map constructed from an aerial photograph is:
options: a map that shows height using contour lines and spot heights
a photograph corrected so that it has a perfectly even scale
a map that shades areas by a statistic such as density
a simplified map showing the main features or land uses
questions.explanation: A précis map summarises a photograph or image by outlining its key features, such as land-use zones, roads and rivers, without the detail. Contour maps show relief and choropleth maps shade areas by value.

questions.stem: Compared with an oblique aerial photograph, a vertical aerial photograph:
options: includes the horizon, so distant features can be compared
has a scale that increases steadily towards the background
shows features from directly above, with a more even scale
shows the sides of buildings, making them easier to identify
questions.explanation: A vertical photo is taken looking straight down, giving a map-like view with a fairly consistent scale that suits measurement. Oblique photos are taken at an angle, show the sides of features and have a scale that changes across the image.
